criterion.summary: No numerical detection threshold is stated in the pipeline paper (1902.10341); its table splits 'events' from 'subthreshold candidates' (FAR ~1/O1, p_astro ~0.15). The companion paper (1902.10331) justifies naming GW151216 by p_astro being above the GWTC-1 bar of 0.5 for listing events. So the effective criterion is p_astro > 0.5 (borrowed from GWTC-1), stated only in 1902.10331 and only for GW151216.
criterion.quote: Our best estimate for the probability that this event is of astrophysical origin yields $P_{\rm astro} \approx 0.7$, which is above the bar of $0.5$ for listing events in the catalog of confident gravitational-wave detections defined in \cite{LIGOScientific:2018mvr}. [...] We therefore adopt the name \CANDIDATE for this event.

below_criterion.notes: Labelled with bare date strings '151231' and '151011' (no GW prefix) in the Name column.

open_questions: 1902.10341 never states a numerical detection threshold; the p_astro > 0.5 bar appears only in 1902.10331 as justification for naming GW151216. Decide whether to record the IAS-O1 criterion as 'p_astro > 0.5 (GWTC-1 bar)' or as 'paper's own events/sub-threshold split'.
Should the bare labels '151231' and '151011' (sub-threshold, p_astro 0.15/0.14) be stored as designations/aliases? They are not detections.
GW151216 IFAR is per-bank (BBH 3); 1902.10331 notes the FAR would be larger after a trials factor over the 5 BBH banks. Abstract says 'one per six years', text says 6.6 yr.
GPS times are 'linear-free' template times, not merger times; offsets from LVC times are expected.
GW150914/GW151012/GW151226 p_astro of 1 are 'effective' values (no credible background density) rather than computed values.
